current_text: Grandmaster Flex leads a quiet round of stretching and breathing. Restore HP.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: "Breathe in. Hold. Breathe out," says Grandmaster Flex.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: "You carry the whole kingdom in your lungs, son. Try not to drop it."

current_text: The Barracks Gauntlet

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Regime recruits drill in the barracks. They are not good at it. They are loud about it.
new_text: You hear the recruits drilling before you see them. They make up in volume what they lack in coordination.

speaker: (narration)

new_text: You face Chancellor Clench's personal guard. Their uniforms are pressed; their technique could use ironing out. (Elite)

current_text: The Trophy Hall

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Trophies of every leader the regime ever overthrew. There is an empty one for Grandmaster Flex.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Chancellor Clench's Gym

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The regime's throne room is a gym with a single throne-shaped bench press. It is the only barbell in the House.

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: Chancellor Clench stands before an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains. It is his.

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: "Master." The word sticks in his throat. "I was your best, you know. Your star pupil."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: "You said I would go further than you ever did. Then you said strength lived in the heart and the head. I knew better."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: "So I took your iron. Your protein. Your followers. And you come back to me weaker than a damp towel."
new_text: "I took your iron, your protein, your followers. You have come back with nothing, Master."
writer_note: Keeps Clench's contempt and list without a damp-towel punchline in the reveal.

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: "Look how far I went, Master. What do you think you can do?"

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: Chancellor Clench falls, bench and all. The regime's banners come down one by one, and in the great hall the Beefcakes begin to cheer, quietly, then very loudly.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: Flex does not gloat. He kneels beside his fallen pupil and offers a hand. "You hated yourself for needing the iron, my boy.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: I never hated you for it. Come back to the gym. We start from zero. Everyone does."

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: Clench has lost his title, his medals and the thing he thought strength was. He stares at the hand a long time. He does not take it yet, but he does not pull away.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: Then Flex turns to you, and his voice is gentle. "Whatever they took from you, son, it was not the part that matters."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: Chancellor Clench stands before an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains. It is his.

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: "A stranger in my house, and no old man at your side. They say Flex is still down in the dark, doing push-ups for nobody."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: "They say he trained a hundred pupils and I was the best of them. Look where that got me. Look where it got him."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
current_text: "Come, then. Let me show you what iron is for."

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: Chancellor Clench falls, bench and all. The regime's banners come down one by one, and in the great hall the Beefcakes begin to cheer, quietly, then very loudly.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: From the stairs come slow, controlled footsteps. Grandmaster Flex walks up out of the Iron-less Prison on his own, in thin grey robes, as if he had popped out for the paper.
new_text: You hear slow, controlled footsteps on the stairs. Grandmaster Flex emerges from the Iron-less Prison alone, in thin grey robes.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: "I was going to leave eventually," he says. "Lovely day for it." Then he looks at his fallen pupil, and his face softens.
new_text: "I was going to leave eventually," he says. His face softens as he looks at his fallen pupil.
writer_note: Keeps the self-rescue variant; removes the weather wink.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: "Get up, my boy. We start from zero. Everyone does."

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
current_text: He glances at you. "Whatever they took from you, son, it was not the part that matters."

current_text: The Calisthenics Check

speaker: (narration)
current_text: No iron in the prison, so the guards test what you can do with your own body. Your first unit must be strong enough to count.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Descent

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The stairway to the Iron-less Prison is steep, dark, and damp. A guard is dozing on the third landing, with a ring of keys on his belt and a bag of confiscated protein bars at his feet.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Sneak past the guard

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Take the bars and the keys (and a bruise)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Do some calming stretches on the stair

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You step lightly. The guard snores on. A heavy door closes behind you, and the cold, iron-less air of the prison settles over you.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The guard wakes just long enough to swing. You leave with the bars, the keys, and a distinct impression of knuckles.
new_text: The guard wakes long enough to swing. You leave with the bars, the keys and a very hands-on reprimand.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Quad stretch, hamstring stretch, shoulder roll. The guard sleeps on. You feel better for it.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Somebody in the dark chuckles approvingly.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Rescue

speaker: (narration)
current_text: In the last cell, a gaunt old man sits cross-legged in the dark, perfectly still. Ten years of breath and calisthenics have worn him down to wire and will.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: He opens one eye. "You are not a guard," he says. "You are far too nervous."
new_text: He opens one eye and looks at you. "You are not a guard."

speaker: (narration)
current_text: There is no bar and no bench, only a patch of stone worn smooth by a decade of training. Ten years, a cell, people trying to break you. Something tightens in your chest, and you do not know why.
new_text: You see no bar or bench, only stone worn smooth by ten years of training. Your chest tightens at the sight of the cell; you do not know why.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Pick the lock and free him

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The lock gives. Grandmaster Flex rises, slowly, unsteadily, and bows. He is so thin you could count his ribs.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: He moves with a stillness that is somehow the opposite of weakness. From now on, he fights beside you.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Trophy Hall

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Trophies of every defeated Beefcake line the walls: belts, medals, the left shoe of a champion.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A single pedestal stands empty, with a plate reading GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). Rude.
new_text: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). The space above it remains empty.

current_text: Take the medals (they are very shiny)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Polish the empty pedestal

speaker: (narration)

current_text: Medals jingle. Grandmaster Flex winces. "They are not ours to take.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Still. The regime owes this house a debt, and gold settles debts." You feel a little guilty, and a little richer.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You polish it until it gleams. Grandmaster Flex watches, and something old and heavy lifts off him. You feel stronger.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Some things are not for taking. Grandmaster Flex nods once, slowly, in approval.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: Careful. The guards come by on the hour. Not the hour of the day. The hour of the squat.
new_text: Careful, son. The guards time their rounds by their squats.
writer_note: Preserves the squat-based patrol without the comic hour riddle.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: It is irregular. Once an hour, whether or not it is an hour.
new_text: The rounds are irregular. Listen for them on the stairs.
writer_note: Retains irregular timing; practical caution in the rescue.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: You're Grandmaster Flex? You're... smaller than the posters.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: Ten years in the dark does that. They took the plates, the protein, the pump. I had nothing.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: So I had everything. My breath. My body. My mind.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: Come, son. We will climb out together. And I would like a word with Clench. He was the best student I ever had.

speaker: Chancellor Clench
current_text: You bring that... that stick of a man into my house? Look at him, Master. Ten years on bread and water.

speaker: Chancellor Clench
current_text: A Beefcake without iron is just a CAKE!

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: Hold my coat.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: They took my weights, Clench. They forgot to take me.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: You only ever took the weight. I taught you the heart, and you stopped listening before I got to the mind.

speaker: Chancellor Clench
current_text: ...What. How. Where were you HIDING all of that?

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: True strength is not the ability to lift heavy things. It comes from the heart, and from the mind.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
current_text: The heavy things were only ever practice. Now, my boy. Shall we?
